value: U.S. Department of Energy, Advanced Manufacturing Office (2017). Bandwidth Study on Energy Use and Potential Energy Saving Opportunities in U.S. Cement Manufacturing. Prepared by Energetics Incorporated (H. Schwartz, N. Ward, B. Levie, B. Chadwell, S. Brueske). Washington, DC: U.S. DOE.

CT -> variant efficiency-base; SOA -> bat; PM -> efficiency-strong (R&D, not commercial). The thermodynamic minimum is a physical floor, not a technology, and sits in _thermodynamic-minimum. PM rows carry the PM lower limit as value and the SOA value as max, since the study defines the PM band as SOA down to the lower limit.
Btu per POUND of the sub-process product (raw meal, fuel, clinker or cement), as printed; 1 Btu/lb = 0.002326 GJ/t.
Dry and wet steps share equipment names (kiln_efficiency-base etc.); the process column distinguishes them, and the example id carries the process.
